text:
Maya: FYI customer (AcmePay) in EMEA reports consistent TLS handshake resets when their corporate proxy sits in front of our hosted endpoints (api.redwood.run). They only see failures for streaming/generation requests. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Alex: Seen it a few times. Common culprits: TLS interception (MITM) that re-signs certs, SNI being stripped/replaced, or proxy downgrading ALPN from h2 to http/1.1. Their logs show `tls alert unknown_ca` and a cut connection during the first server push.

Priya: Customer claims their proxy enforces SNI-based routing + forces HTTP/1.1 for compatibility. They also do header rewriting for Host to internal hostnames.

Jordan: Important: our public LB relies on TLS SNI for proper routing and ALPN for HTTP/2 streaming. If the proxy terminates TLS and re-issues a certificate, or strips SNI/ALPN, our streaming SSE/chunked semantics can break. Also long-lived connections can be torn down if proxy idle timeout is low.

Maya: They asked if they can just whitelist IPs instead of hostnames. We have region-specific NAT pools and they rotate. We should give guidance: FQDN + CONNECT + port 443 preferred; if IPs are required, provide ranges with caveat about drift and update window.

Alex: Recommend customer do one of the following (ordered):
- Configure proxy to allow `CONNECT` passthrough for `api.redwood.run:443` and not terminate TLS for that host (i.e., preserve SNI).
- If TLS inspection is mandatory, ensure the proxy preserves SNI header and ALPN (`h2`) and does not rewrite `Host` header.
- If they must whitelist IPs, allow our published region NAT ranges and a buffer for rotation (we'll provide latest list).

Priya: Quick repro command you can share with their infra team:
```
# test CONNECT passthrough via corporate proxy
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.run/v1/health
```
If this fails with a cert mismatch or `unknown_ca` it's likely TLS inspection.

Sam C.S.: From CS: they want a minimal checklist we can send to customer. Also asked whether Dedicated/Private would avoid this.

Jordan: Dedicated/private helps: Dedicated can be placed in a customer VPC or private peering, avoiding customer outbound proxies entirely. But it has procurement/time/cost implications. For hosted customers, best-effort guidance:
- Whitelist `api.redwood.run` (443) and allow `CONNECT` method.
- Preserve SNI and ALPN, do not rewrite Host header.
- Idle timeout >= 300s for streaming requests and token polling.
- Allow long-lived TLS connections; don't recycle connection after every request.

Alex: If IP whitelist required, give them these example ranges (note: these can change):
- us-east NAT pool: 34.200.120.0/20
- eu-west NAT pool: 35.180.64.0/19
- ap-south NAT pool: 36.140.0.0/18
Explain we publish updates on a weekly cadence to their security contact and they should allow a 72hr window for changes.

Priya: Also call out proxy auth: if their proxy requires Basic/NTLM auth, clients must set `HTTPS_PROXY` with creds; our SDKs respect `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` env vars but do not implement NTLM by default.

Maya: Edge case noted: some proxies downgrade to HTTP/1.1 and buffer chunked responses which breaks our streaming `chunked`-style generator responses. If they can't passthrough, ask them to enable HTTP/2 ALPN support on the proxy for TLS-forwarded hosts.

ops-bot: NOTE: NAT IP pools may be rotated. See docs: https://docs.redwood.run/networking/egress-ip-pools (we push updates to `account-security@redwood.com`).

Sam C.S.: I'll draft a short outbound checklist for them with exact curl tests and request their proxy vendor and version. Also asking whether we can provide a temporary region-specific IP allowlist while they coordinate with SecOps.

Jordan: Action items:
1) Priya/Sam: send checklist + curl snippets and ask for proxy vendor/version and whether TLS inspection is enabled.
2) Maya/Alex: compile current NAT ranges and note rotation cadence; add note about ALPN/SNI requirements.
3) If customer wants, propose Dedicated trial and include cost/time estimate.

Maya: Thanks all. I'll add a short blurb to the support template about `SNI preservation + ALPN h2 + CONNECT` as a must for hosted streaming endpoints. :thumbsup:

Alex: FYI we should also add a small troubleshooting script to our runbook to detect TLS interception (check cert chain issuer vs public CA) and HTTP/2 negotiation.

Priya: pinging @Sam C.S. for customer-facing follow-up.

Sam C.S.: On it — will update thread when I have proxy details.
